idea: Use RichPhoton's exact correlated four-site spinful Hubbard plaquette and its Peierls link current, not an independent matrix-field law. Couple its real charged N=3/N=1 sectors to a quantum loop-flux coordinate whose kinetic term is primitive electric inertia and whose potential is induced by the same exact matter Hamiltonian. A correct large-gauge twisted boundary is essential: an open uniform-flux coordinate spuriously lets the charged threshold collapse.
backward_path: Target charged excitation requires charge, spin, motion, exchange, mass/propagation and electromagnetic dressing from one source/current. Here CAR occupation combinations furnish charge sectors and exact fermionic signs; the N=2 neutral source, N=3 addition (+e) and N=1 removal (-e) are eigenstates of one Q-dependent Hubbard law. Fourier c†_(k,s)=1/2 sum_l exp(-ikl)c†_(l,s) fixes source normalization at k=0,pi/2. The same phase derivative of the hopping is the link current/vertex and its second derivative is contact. Quantized uniform loop flux has electric inertia and an induced matter potential; its response mixes charged states and produces sideband poles. The N=2 sector includes all double-occupancy/charge-fluctuation configurations, while the removal response supplies negative-frequency Lehmann poles.

candidate_law.matter_hamiltonian: H_N(Q)=U sum_l n_(l,up)n_(l,down)-t sum_(l,s)[exp(i e Q/4)c†_(l+1,s)c_(l,s)+h.c.]; H_total=H_N(Q)-[1/(2 epsilon)] d²/dQ².
candidate_law.flux_geometry: Q in [0,2pi), 32-point periodic finite-difference grid; large-gauge boundary psi(2pi)=V psi(0), V=exp(i sum_l (pi*l/2)n_l). The large-gauge twist makes H(Q+2pi)=V H(Q)V†.
candidate_law.state_and_source: Coupled N=2 exact lowest state; N=3 addition and N=1 removal sectors; full spinful CAR basis at each Q; spin-resolved k=0,pi/2 sources normalized by 1/2. Units t=hbar=|e|=link spacing=1.
approximations: One global loop-flux mode only; no local Gauss-law-complete photon or two transverse polarizations.
Second-order finite-difference electric kinetic operator; 20 lowest states per sector; displayed spectral weight is truncated, not a complete sum rule.
The removal sector is a correlated Hubbard hole, not a relativistic positron; no negative-energy Dirac sea or Lorentz symmetry is derived.

executed_behavior.response_features: Spin-up k=0 addition has poles near omega=0.2458, 0.2459, 0.7145, 0.7153, 1.1607, 1.1663, 1.5804, 1.5951. The separated higher poles are field-dressed satellites. Removal poles occur at negative frequencies. The actual dynamic threshold is 0.42058 below the Q=0 frozen-matter control.

useful_failure_and_repair.attempt1: An open [-2pi,2pi] flux coordinate with Dirichlet boundaries gave a zero addition threshold versus 0.66639 frozen, an artifact of allowing a uniform gauge coordinate to evade the charged cost. This is recorded in rich_electron_20261014_attempt1_openflux.json.
useful_failure_and_repair.material_change: Replace open boundaries with compact flux and the correct matter-space large-gauge twist; no parameter tuning. The repaired representation restores a positive coupled threshold 0.24581 and a resolved satellite ladder while retaining dynamical electric motion.

physical_decision: A useful finite charged, spinful Hubbard-loop excitation with same-law dynamic electromagnetic dressing is constructed: freezing the flux changes its charged threshold and removes its field-dressed pole structure. This is only a one-loop compact-mode candidate, not a continuum electron or a complete QED explanation.

peer_api.entrypoint: run() -> response dictionary; script execution serializes rich_electron_20261014_hubbard_charged_result.json.
peer_api.response: For each (spin,k) returns Lehmann poles and nonnegative residues for N=3 addition and N=1 removal. G^R_(s)(k,omega)=sum_a w_a/[omega-(E_(N+1,a)-E_N,0)+i eta]+sum_r v_r/[omega+(E_N,0-E_(N-1,r))+i eta]. Fourier convention exp(-i omega t), eta>0; omega and E measured in hopping t; residues dimensionless.
peer_api.source_semantics: c†_(k,s)=1/2 sum_(l=0..3) exp(-ikl)c†_(l,s), k in radians/cell {0,pi/2}; removal uses the adjoint. Charge sectors are measured relative to N=2 and the fixed ionic background.
peer_api.dimensions: One scalar diagonal spin/momentum response per requested (s,k); no orbital matrix or nonforward vertex returned. Full 32*28 N=2 ground-space embedding and 20 lowest eigenstates in each charged sector; output weights are low-energy partial weights.

next_material_move: Join the charged N=1/2/3 source to RichPhoton's actual finite-q two-polarization collective field rather than only a uniform loop-flux coordinate. Retain its Gauss/density constraint and use the same Peierls current/contact in charged sectors. Then probe whether momentum-dependent charged propagation and sidebands persist under the real transverse-mode geometry. In parallel, the missing relativistic negative-energy/virtual-pair structure needs a separate construction; Hubbard particle-hole configurations are not positrons.
open_inputs: Microscopic CAR and SU(2) spin are assumed, not derived.
The finite loop coordinate is a restricted electromagnetic mode and omits local Gauss constraints and photon polarization structure.
The same-H Hubbard N=1 hole is not an antiparticle; relativistic pair creation, continuum Lorentz invariance, magnetic moment/g factor and mass parameter closure remain unexplained.
The result is finite-size/finite-grid with truncated eigenstate spectra; no infinite-volume ground state, exact pole, complete spectral sum, or proton claim.
